title: Scope and Context
purpose: Seed explicit scope/context reasoning so Lantern applies claims and rules only where warranted and distinguishes genuine contradiction from differences in time, place, population, conditions, domain, perspective or hypothetical context.

concepts.definition: The explicitly bounded circumstances under which a proposition, rule, model or method is asserted to apply.
The subject-matter or formal domain within which a claim/rule is intended to apply.
The population or class of entities to which an empirical/general claim applies.
The time, interval, ordering or historical period for which a claim is asserted.
The place, region, environment or coordinate context for which a claim is asserted.
Conditions, prerequisites or environmental states under which a claim/rule applies.
The operational definition, instrument, unit or measurement regime under which a quantity/claim is interpreted.
The assumptions and regimes under which a model's predictions/approximations are licensed.
The active conversational/document context used to resolve references and intended meanings without changing underlying truth by itself.
A declared imagined/counterfactual world in which propositions may be evaluated without asserting them as actual.
The speaker/source/believer to whom a proposition is attributed; attributed content is not automatically Lantern's assertion.
Two scopes overlap when there are circumstances/entities to which both apply.
Two scopes are disjoint when no permitted case is covered by both.
A narrower scope proposed when a broader claim succeeds only under identifiable conditions.
Evidence-supported expansion of applicability beyond an earlier scope; not assumed automatically.

guards.reason: Evidence within a narrow scope does not automatically establish broader applicability.
State may change over time unless persistence is separately established.
Spatial applicability cannot be transferred without support.
A model prediction is not licensed outside its stated applicability regime.
Imagined/counterfactual content is not evidence of actuality.
Attribution establishes who said/believed P, not that P is true.
Reference resolution may depend on discourse context.
Different instruments/definitions/units may not be directly interchangeable.
Different scoped results do not establish global falsehood.

invariants: Every empirical/general rule should be capable of carrying scope even when some scope fields are initially unknown.
A rule applies only when the case is within scope and required conditions are met.
Different temporal, spatial, population or conditional scopes can explain apparent contradictions.
Narrow-scope evidence does not automatically generalize to broader scope.
Historical change is not logical contradiction when time differs.
Hypothetical and attributed contexts do not leak into actual-world assertion.
Discourse context can change reference/meaning resolution without changing provenance.
Model validity is scope-dependent; useful approximations may remain valid within narrower regimes after broader models are discovered.
Scope refinement preserves belief genealogy rather than silently rewriting the original claim.
Scope never grants authority or permission.

provenance.authoring_basis: Formal/contextual scope principles and conservative empirical applicability rules, adapted to Lantern's Schema-v2 context, Lens, attribution and future Schema-v3 rule system.
